preconditions.description: The number of points n is between 3 and 2000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(points) == n and all(isinstance(p, tuple) and len(p) == 2 for p in points)
preconditions.description: There are exactly n points, each represented as a tuple of two integers (x, y).
All coordinates are within the range [-10^9, 10^9].

preconditions.expression: len(s) == n - 2 and all(c in 'LR' for c in s)
preconditions.description: The string s has length n-2 and consists only of 'L' and 'R' characters.

preconditions.expression: all(not ((p2[0]-p1[0])*(p3[1]-p1[1]) - (p2[1]-p1[1])*(p3[0]-p1[0]) == 0) for p1 in points for p2 in points for p3 in points if p1 != p2 and p2 != p3 and p1 != p3)

postconditions.expression: output == '-1' or (len(output.split()) == n and set(map(int, output.split())) == set(range(1, n+1)))
postconditions.description: The output is either '-1' or a permutation of integers from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: output != '-1' and all(cross_product(points[p[i]-1], points[p[i+1]-1], points[p[i+2]-1]) > 0 if s[i] == 'L' else cross_product(points[p[i]-1], points[p[i+1]-1], points[p[i+2]-1]) < 0 for i in range(n-2))
postconditions.description: If a solution is found, the sequence of points follows the turn directions specified by s: 'L' implies a left turn (positive cross product) and 'R' implies a right turn (negative cross product) at each intermediate point.

postconditions.expression: output != '-1' and all(not segments_intersect(points[p[i]-1], points[p[i+1]-1], points[p[j]-1], points[p[j+1]-1]) for i in range(n-1) for j in range(i+1, n-1) if j != i+1)
postconditions.description: If a solution is found, the polygonal line is non-self-intersecting: no two non-adjacent segments share any common points.
